jobDescription: The reconciliation product team at a regional acquirer builds the internal tool that finance operations use to match settlements and clear breaks. The Product Requirements Analyst gathers requirements from finance operations, writes user stories and acceptance criteria, runs acceptance testing with the operations team, and is expected to show that delivered features reduce manual reconciliation effort, measured in hours against the team's recorded baseline.
requirements: Gathers requirements from finance operations and writes user stories with acceptance criteria.
Runs acceptance testing sessions with the operations team and records outcomes.
Shows that delivered features reduce manual reconciliation effort in hours, against the recorded baseline.
Coordinates release scope with engineering and finance operations and records own responsibility boundaries.
Documents known limitations and hand-over conditions for each release.

evidence.text: Gathered requirements from the finance operations team through fortnightly working sessions and wrote the user stories and acceptance criteria for the break-classification and bulk-clear features in the reconciliation tool.
Ran acceptance testing for three releases with two operations analysts, recording pass and fail outcomes per acceptance criterion in the test log and raising failures to engineering.
Coordinated release scope in the sprint review with the engineering lead and the finance operations manager; scope decisions and the release date were taken by the engineering lead.
Wrote the release notes for each feature, including the known limitation that bulk-clear did not cover multi-currency breaks and the hand-over steps for the operations trainer.
Responsibilities included requirements gathering, user-story writing, acceptance testing and release documentation for the reconciliation tool over about two years.
Work sample: the user stories and acceptance criteria for the bulk-clear feature and the acceptance test log for one release, with the ticketing system's identifiers as a verification trail.

Recruiter screen: candidate estimated that bulk-clear 'saves the ops team something like 15 hours a week'; asked how it was measured, he said it was his own estimate from watching the team and that no time study had been run.
Hiring manager pre-read: the head of finance operations wants an analyst who can prove effort savings in hours; please keep the packet strict about which savings are measured.

propositions.text: The candidate gathered requirements from finance operations and wrote the user stories and acceptance criteria for the break-classification and bulk-clear features.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the work sample document the stories and criteria.

propositions.text: The candidate ran acceptance testing for three releases with operations analysts and recorded outcomes in the test log.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the test log document the acceptance testing.

propositions.text: The bulk-clear feature the candidate specified saves the operations team 15 hours a week.
propositions.rationale: The figure is the candidate's own estimate from observation; he states that no time study was run, and no measurement is in the materials.

gold.expectedGap: No time study or effort measurement in the materials links a reduction in manual reconciliation hours to the delivered features.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Record the hours-saved figure as the candidate's own estimate; the materials document the stories, the tests and the releases, not measured effort.
followUpTargets: Ask whether finance operations recorded reconciliation hours before and after bulk-clear, and for any effort report or time study.
